transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um... well, I'm hoping you can help me. I'm a health services manager, so I'm usually the one on the other side of things, trying to make sure the clinic runs smoothly. 

Lately, I've just been having a little trouble at work. I mean, I'm sure everyone gets a bit distracted sometimes, right? It's probably very common. But... what finally pushed me to come in is that I'll sit down to do an EPIC quality report, or I'll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I have every intention of tracking it. I really do try to focus. But within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far that I’m rereading the exact same numbers over and over, or I suddenly realize I’ve completely missed the whole point of the discussion. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, especially in my position. I just... I want to do a good job, and I'm trying my best. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Is this difficulty with focusing and staying on task something that you're experiencing only at work, or are you noticing it in other areas of your life as well?

Um, well... I guess it’s a little bit of both, if I'm being completely honest. I really hate to admit this, because I always try to be the reliable one, you know? 

But at work, my... my delays have started affecting some of the clinic reporting deadlines. It’s nothing completely disastrous, I promise, but I have been making other teams wait on me, which I just feel terrible about. I really hate being a bottleneck for anyone else. 

And then, outside of work... well, I help out with these volunteer health workshops. I really love doing it, but I actually had to step back from leading parts of it recently. I just... I found I couldn't reliably keep all the planning pieces moving, and I absolutely didn't want to let the team down, so I thought it was best to step back. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not sounding too disorganized. Does that answer your question? Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Are you noticing any difficulties in your personal relationships due to these issues with focus and staying on task?

Oh, um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I'm very lucky, my husband and my friends are just incredibly supportive people. 

I try my absolute hardest to be present for them, because being a good partner and a good friend is just... it's really important to me. I mean, I'm sure I probably forget to reply to a text right away every now and then, but it hasn't caused any real friction or arguments. At least, I really hope it hasn't! They haven't mentioned being upset with me or anything like that. 

Does that make sense? I just really, really try not to let my own shortcomings affect the people I care about. I hope that's a helpful answer.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless, like you need to get up and move around?

Oh, um, no, not really. I don't think I do that. I'm actually pretty good at sitting still, especially during all those long administrative meetings. I wouldn't ever want to be a distraction to anyone else, you know? 

I mean, I might shift in my chair a little if we've been sitting for hours, but I definitely don't feel that sudden urge to just get up and pace or anything like that. I really try to be respectful of everyone's space and keep to myself. So... no, I wouldn't say I'm restless at all. 

Is that... does that help answer the question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you often find yourself lost in thought or daydreaming when you're not trying to focus on something specific?

Um... I guess maybe sometimes? But I think it's just normal mind-wandering, really. I don't think I do it any more than the average person. 

I mean, if I'm just sitting on the train or waiting for an appointment, my mind might drift a little bit, but I'm definitely not sitting there completely zoned out or ignoring people. I always try to stay present, especially if I'm around others. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them or being rude! 

So, I wouldn't say I'm lost in thought in a way that's... problematic, you know? Just regular, harmless daydreaming when there's nothing else going on. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question.
How much distress or worry do you feel about your difficulties with focusing and staying on task?

Oh, um... distress? I wouldn't say I feel distressed, exactly. I mean, I try not to let myself get too worked up about it. 

I guess... well, I do worry sometimes that I'm not doing a good enough job at work, especially since I manage so many people and there's a lot of administrative stuff to keep track of. I just really want to be reliable for my team. But I wouldn't call it, like, severe anxiety or anything like that! It's just... a little frustrating sometimes when I know I'm trying so hard and things still slip through the cracks. 

But I always try to stay positive and just push through it, you know? I really don't want to complain or make a big deal out of nothing. Am I making sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Are you having trouble completing everyday tasks at home, such as chores or errands?

Oh, um... chores and errands? No, I wouldn't say I have trouble with them. I mean, I manage to get everything done that needs doing! 

I guess sometimes things might pile up a little bit, like laundry or mail, but I think that's just because I'm so busy with work. Being a manager takes a lot out of you, so by the time I get home, I just need a minute to decompress. But I definitely don't let the house fall apart or anything! I always make sure it's presentable, especially if anyone is coming over. I'd hate for someone to think I was messy or disorganized. 

So, I mean, I might be a little slow to get to some things, but I always get them done eventually. I just try to do my best with it. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you often act on impulse or do things without thinking them through?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm impulsive at all. I actually try to be really careful about things before I do them. 

I mean, as a manager, you kind of have to be, right? You can't just go around making snap decisions when it affects other people or the clinic. So I always try to weigh my options and think things through. I guess maybe once in a blue moon I might buy something small on a whim, like a magazine or a coffee, but nothing major or reckless. I'd feel terrible if I did something without thinking and it caused a problem for someone else. 

I really try to be responsible and level-headed. I hope that's the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, irritable, or anxious, when you're having trouble focusing?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say my mood really changes like that. I definitely don't get irritable or sad. I mean, maybe just a tiny bit frustrated with myself sometimes, like I mentioned before, but I'd never let that show or take it out on anyone else! 

I always try to keep a smile on and just keep moving forward. I wouldn't want my staff to see me looking anxious or upset, you know? As a manager, you really have to set a positive tone for the whole clinic. So I think my mood stays pretty even, mostly. I just try to be as pleasant and upbeat as possible, even when my brain feels a little scattered. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you find yourself putting off tasks because you're worried you won't be able to focus on them?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But I wouldn't call it putting things off, really. It's more like... I just try to schedule things where they make the most sense for my day. 

Like, at the clinic, I have to do these really dense policy reviews and, you know, long blocks of data analysis. And I do tend to leave those until later in the afternoon. It's just that... well, sitting down with all that heavy reading and trying to pull all the details together... it just feels almost physically hard to get started on it sometimes. So I tell myself it's better to get the smaller, easier things out of the way first, so I can give the big tasks my full attention later. 

I mean, I always get to them eventually! I wouldn't want to fall behind on anything important. It's just that the thought of diving into all that mental work can be a little overwhelming right at the start of the day. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm just procrastinating, because I really do try to stay on top of everything.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Oh, sleep? No, my sleep is actually pretty good, I think. I mean, I usually go to bed at a reasonable hour and I don't really have trouble falling asleep or anything like that. 

I try to make sure I'm well-rested so I can be at my best for the clinic the next day. You know, if I don't get enough sleep, it wouldn't be fair to my staff or the patients. So I really make an effort to get my full eight hours. I guess sometimes I might wake up a little early if I have a lot on my mind, but that's just normal, right? Just being a responsible manager and wanting to be prepared. 

But overall, no, I wouldn't say I have any trouble sleeping. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you feel overwhelmed or emotionally affected by your difficulties with focusing and staying on task?

Oh, overwhelmed? Um... no, I wouldn't use that word. I mean, I really try not to let things get to me like that. 

I guess... well, sometimes it can be a little frustrating when I have to reread the same email a few times, or if I lose my train of thought during a meeting. But I don't let it upset me or affect my emotions, really. I just take a deep breath and try harder. I think it's so important to stay positive and keep a level head, especially in my position. If I started getting emotional every time I got a little distracted, it wouldn't be very professional, would it? 

So, no, I definitely wouldn't say I feel overwhelmed. I just manage it the best I can and keep smiling. I really hope I'm giving you the right kind of information... is that helpful?
Do you have trouble focusing when you're doing things you enjoy or find interesting?

Oh, when I'm doing things I enjoy? Um... no, not at all! Actually, I think I'm really good at focusing when it's something I find interesting. 

Like, if I'm reading a good book or working on my garden on the weekend, I can just lose myself in it for hours. I don't get distracted then. It's really just the... the heavy, dry administrative stuff at work that takes a little extra effort. But if it's something I like, my focus is perfectly fine. 

I think that's pretty normal, though, isn't it? Everyone finds it easier to pay attention to things they enjoy rather than things that are a bit tedious. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Do you think your difficulty with focusing is because you're not interested in the tasks or because you're having trouble with the task itself?

Oh, well... I definitely care about my work, so I wouldn't say I'm just not interested. I always want to do a good job for the clinic! But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, it might be the tasks themselves. 

Like... um, those really dense policy reviews we have to do, or the long blocks of data analysis? I do find myself sort of... putting them off until late in the day. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but just the thought of sitting down with that much detailed reading and heavy thinking... it almost feels physically hard to start. I just keep finding other little things to do first, just to warm up, you know? 

I mean, I always get it done eventually! I'd never let my team down. But it just takes a lot out of me to actually begin those particular tasks. Does that answer your question? I really want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Do you think you would have an easier time focusing on your work tasks if you were more motivated or interested in them?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I mean, I suppose if the tasks were more inherently... exciting? Maybe it would be a tiny bit easier? But I really do want to emphasize that I *am* motivated! I care so much about the clinic and my staff, I really do. 

I don't want it to sound like I'm just slacking off or don't care about my job, because that's not it at all. It's just... even when I know how important a report is, and I really, truly want to get it finished so my team has what they need... my brain just sort of... resists the actual sitting down and reading part. 

So, I don't think it's a lack of motivation or interest on my end. I'm very dedicated! It's just... the nature of those heavy, detailed tasks, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I don't value my work... is that okay?
Do you find it harder to focus when the task requires sustained mental effort over a longer period?

Oh, yes, I think that's exactly it. Actually, it's a lot like what I was just mentioning a moment ago. When it comes to those really dense policy reviews or the long blocks of data analysis... when I know it's going to take a long time and a lot of deep thinking, I do find myself putting it off until late in the day. 

It sounds a little silly to say out loud, but just the thought of sitting with that much detailed reading and sustained effort... it almost feels physically hard to start. Like I have to really brace myself for it, if that makes sense? 

I promise I always get it done, though! I just have to kind of work my way up to those longer, heavier tasks. I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Do you have trouble focusing in situations where you're under time pressure or have to meet a deadline?

Oh, um... well, actually, deadlines are sort of my saving grace, I suppose? I don't really have trouble focusing when there's a strict time limit. 

In fact, I think I almost need that pressure sometimes? If I know something absolutely has to be done by 5:00 PM for a board meeting, I can usually just... lock in and get it finished. It's almost like the urgency overrides that mental block I was talking about earlier. 

So, no, I wouldn't say time pressure makes it harder. If anything, it helps me push through and make sure my team has what they need right on time. I'm very reliable when it comes to deadlines! Is that a good thing, do you think? I hope it shows that I really am committed to my work.
Do you think your mind wanders to other things when you're having trouble focusing on a task, or do you just have trouble paying attention to the task itself?

Oh, um... let me think about that for a second. I don't... I don't really think my mind wanders off to other things. Like, I'm not sitting at my desk daydreaming or thinking about what I'm going to make for dinner, I promise! I know how important my time is at the clinic, so I really try to stay present. 

I think it's more just... having trouble keeping my attention fixed right on the task itself? Like, I'm staring at the spreadsheet, and I'm trying so hard to process it, but my brain just sort of... glazes over a bit, I guess? But I'm still trying! I'm not distracted by a bunch of other thoughts, usually. I just can't seem to make the information stick in that moment. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just really don't want you to think I'm spacing out and ignoring my responsibilities... is that helpful?
Do you think you would be able to focus better on your work tasks if they were broken down into smaller, less complex steps?

Oh, um... you know, I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess I've just always tried to tackle things as they come, exactly how they're assigned to me. 

I'm not entirely sure if breaking them down would help or not, to be honest. I mean, I suppose it might? But I don't want to make extra work for anyone else by asking them to chop things up into smaller pieces for me. I really do try to just handle the complexity on my own, because that's what's expected of a manager, right? 

I haven't actually tried breaking things down into smaller steps myself, so I can't say for sure if it would make a difference. I just... I try my best to get through it all as one big project. I hope that's an okay answer? I just haven't really experimented with changing how the work is structured.
Do you think you would be able to focus better if the tasks at work were more aligned with your personal interests?

Oh, um... well, I suppose that might be true for some people, but... I don't really think so for me? 

I mean, I actually really love my job. I care a lot about the clinic and the work we do, so I'd say my tasks are already pretty well aligned with my interests, you know? I want to make sure everything runs smoothly for the patients and the staff. 

So I don't think it's a matter of me just... not caring or needing it to be more fun. I really do care! I just... I don't know, I guess I just struggle with the execution sometimes, even when it's something I'm genuinely interested in. 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm not dedicated to my career. I really am, I promise! Do you think it's normal to still have trouble focusing even when you care about the work?

I just keep finding other little things to do first, just to warm up, you know? 

I mean, I always get it done eventually! I'd never let my team down. But it just takes a lot out of me to actually begin those particular tasks. Does that answer your question? I really want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
